entities.summary: Laudabiliter was a bull issued in 1155 by Pope Adrian IV, the only Englishman to have served in that office. Existence of the bull has been disputed by scholars over the centuries; no copy is extant but scholars cite the many references to it as early as the 13th century to support the validity of its existence. The bull grants the right to the Angevin King Henry II of England to invade and govern Ireland and to enforce the Gregorian Reforms on the semi-autonomous Christian Church in Ireland. Richard de Clare ("Strongbow") and the other leaders of the Anglo-Norman invasion of Ireland (1169–1171) claimed that Laudabiliter authorised the invasion.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Laudabiliter's authorization of Henry II's invasion of Ireland had significant regional impact on the Anglo-Norman settlement and the development of Christianity in Ireland. The bull's provisions also influenced the establishment of English rule in Ireland, shaping its history for centuries.
